title: Israel's Remilk makes real milk protein with yeast, without cows, and brought it to cafés and shelves

trailer.text: Remilk is an Israeli company founded in 2019 by entrepreneur Aviv Wolff and biochemist Dr. Ori Cohavi.
Its researchers insert the gene for a milk protein into yeast, and the yeast produces it in fermentation tanks.
In 2023 the company received a first-of-its-kind approval from the Israeli Ministry of Health to market non-animal dairy products in Israel, after approvals in the US and Singapore.
With Gad Dairies it launched New Milk, a lactose-free milk whose protein is made in tanks and not in a cow.
According to Ynet, about 600 thousand bottles had been sold by June 2026.

stations.title: Two founders and a grandfather with cows

paragraphs.text: Aviv Wolff entered entrepreneurship after eight years of service as an officer in an elite military unit and after a career in cybersecurity.
He also has a personal connection to milk: his grandfather was a dairy farmer.
Alongside him was Ori Cohavi, who holds a PhD in biochemistry and became CTO.
The two were in the first cohort of the JumpTAU accelerator at Tel Aviv University's entrepreneurship center.
In 2019 they founded Remilk.
Wolff set a big goal.
According to him, if the company reproduces taste, nutritional value and functionality at an affordable price, the use of the cow will end.
According to Green Queen, Americans today drink about 40% less milk than in the 1970s.
According to the same source, lactose intolerance is especially common in Black and Asian communities and also among Ashkenazi Jews.
According to Remilk, its products are real milk made without cows.
According to the company, they contain no lactose, cholesterol, antibiotics or growth hormones.
Remilk also estimates that its process uses only a small fraction of the land, water and emissions of regular milk.

stations.title: The invention: yeast that makes milk protein

paragraphs.text: According to Times of Israel, Remilk produces milk proteins in a yeast-based fermentation process.
It takes the genes that encode the milk proteins and inserts them into a single-cell microbe.
The researchers start with beta-lactoglobulin, a major whey protein.
They insert into the yeast the gene sequence that contains the instructions for producing it.
According to the FDA letter, the gene is synthesized and encodes a protein identical to that of the domestic cow.
In the fermentation tanks the yeast receives sugar and nutrients, and it produces the protein.
According to the FDA letter, the protein is released from the yeast into the surrounding liquid and is separated from them in several filtration steps.
It is then dried into a powder, from which many products can be made.
According to Cohavi, the team took a technology that has been used for decades to produce small quantities of vitamins and enzymes, and operated it on a large scale.
It was followed by a $120 million round.
According to AgFunderNews, the company originally planned a large fermentation facility in Denmark.
According to Ynet, the plan was put on hold, and the company chose to use existing production capacity in Europe.
Today, according to Ynet, the protein is made by a third-party producer in Spain.
According to Green Queen, in January

stations.title: The approvals: US, Singapore, Israel, Canada

paragraphs.text: The US FDA received the GRAS notice submitted on behalf of Remilk on March 8, 2022, and filed it on June 30, 2022.
The notice concerned the use of the protein as a source of protein at levels of 5% to 35% in food.
Remilk included an analysis of three non-consecutive batches to show that it produces the protein to specification.
According to Remilk, as quoted in the letter, the yeast contains no antibiotic resistance genes.
According to the company, the yeast proteins remain in the final product in an amount of less than 0.15%.
The FDA wrote that it has no questions at this time about Remilk's conclusion.

According to Green Queen, California-based Perfect Day was the first company to earn GRAS status for precision fermentation β-lactoglobulin, about two years before Remilk became the second company to receive a no-questions letter from the FDA.
According to a Globes report from June 2022, Remilk received self-affirmed GRAS status, and it is the first Israeli company in the dairy alternatives sector to obtain FDA approval.
In early 2024 approval also came from Health Canada.
According to Wolff, the Israeli approval is a defining moment for Remilk, for the alternative protein industry and for the State of Israel.
Prime Minister Netanyahu said in a statement that the technology will strengthen the economy, food security and animal welfare, and will help in dealing with the climate crisis.
According to FoodNavigator, in July 2022 Remilk announced a large-scale commercial agreement with CBC, the exclusive Israeli franchisee of Coca-Cola.
Later it announced a partnership with Gad Dairies.
Together they launched New Milk.
New Milk is a low-sugar, lactose-free milk.
According to Times of Israel, it has 75% less sugar than regular milk and is fortified with calcium and vitamins.
It has less protein than regular milk, and no casein.
The product first went out to cafés, restaurants and hotels in Israel.
The retail launches were scheduled for January 2026.
According to AgFunderNews, it will sell at a premium price, like plant-based milk alternatives.
According to a survey by Remilk and Gad, 66% of Israelis separate meat and dairy according to kosher dietary laws.
According to Wolff, the products are good news for those who keep kosher: they can drink coffee with parve milk after a meat meal.
According to Ynet, about 600 thousand bottles had been sold by June 2026, with revenue of about 7 million shekels.

stations.title: What did not work, and who it does not suit

paragraphs.text: According to FoodNavigator, the obstacles facing the industry are raising investment, scaling up production and obtaining approvals.
According to AgFunderNews, venture capital funds were reluctant to fund large projects, and banks were unwilling to finance technology not yet proven in the market.
According to Ynet, the large facility in Denmark was put on hold.
A planned partnership with the dairy company Tara also did not go ahead.
The company is in talks to begin selling in the US.
According to Ynet, as of August 2026 a full commercial launch there had not yet been announced.

According to Wolf, even before reaching large-scale production the company is seeing high positive margins ("growth margins", in his words) and very competitive prices because of the efficiency of its process.
The products are not suitable for people who are allergic to milk, because this is real milk protein.
Remilk spokeswoman Barbara Marks said the product is safe for people who are lactose intolerant but not for people who are allergic to milk.
According to the FDA, an allergen warning must be placed on the label.
According to Remilk, the protein is not intended for infant formula.
The FDA also noted that it did not consider whether section 301(ll) of the Act applies to foods containing the protein.
